weakRandomness.notes: None. block.timestamp is used only as an accrual clock (lastRewardTime), never as entropy for a value-bearing selection.

inboundCallbackSurface.notes: No ERC721/1155 receive hooks, no _safeMint. Inbound callback surface is (a) the owner-set IPhlimboHook (onDeposit/onWithdraw/onClaim, called LAST after all state writes) and (b) any transfer hook in the owner-set promoToken / rewardToken.

story024GateAssessment.verdict: The gate closes ALL THREE flush-reachable accrual paths (collectReward, setDesiredAPY-commit, setDepletionDuration) at the single accrual site. accPromoPerShare provably cannot advance while promoPhase == Flushing. beginFlush's final accrual is preserved (it runs while phase is still Active). The V3-H-01 root cause is closed at the accrual site and the fix is site-based rather than caller-based, so it is future-proof against new call sites.
story024GateAssessment.residual: The gate skips promo accrual but lastRewardTime STILL advances to block.timestamp (L767) — the promo stream's elapsed time is shared with the stable/phUSD streams and is not preserved. Consequence is path-dependent and only material on the abortFlush path. See LOCAL-001.

claimedVsActualInvariants.claimed: Pausing blocks all whenNotPaused ops, so from this point every user's amount (except pauseWithdraw, which realigns debts) and the staker set are frozen.

'every user's amount frozen except pauseWithdraw' holds literally, but the parenthetical understates the consequence: pauseWithdraw also mutates totalStaked mid-flush without calling _updatePool, which mis-scales the NEXT stable/phUSD accrual across the whole stale window. The comment frames pauseWithdraw as fully self-neutralising ('realigns debts'), which is true for the actor but not for co-stakers.

localFindings.description: The story-024 phase gate skips promo accrual during Flushing but lastRewardTime is still advanced to block.timestamp at L767 (it is shared with the stable and phUSD streams, so it cannot simply be held back). The promo stream therefore has no clock of its own. Consequence: whether the flush window's promo accrues at all depends on whether ANY third party calls the permissionless collectReward during the flush. If nobody does, lastRewardTime stays at beginFlush's timestamp and the FULL flush window accrues retroactively on the first post-abortFlush _updatePool. If anyone calls collectReward(1 wei) during the flush, that window's promo time is silently discarded for every staker. A griefer can therefore burn the promo accrual window for all stakers for the cost of one collectReward call.
localFindings.impact: Bounded. promoRewardBalance is NOT decremented when the gate skips, so no tokens are lost — the remainder simply streams later over a stretched wall-clock window (the rate is not recomputed). Material only on the abortFlush path; on the normal finalizePromotion path the retired stream's leftover is swept anyway. No insolvency; INV-5's solvency claim is untouched.
localFindings.recommendation: Give the promo stream its own promoLastRewardTime, or snapshot lastRewardTime at beginFlush and restore it at abortFlush, so the freeze is time-preserving rather than time-discarding.
localFindings.deferTo: econ-scanner (is the stretched window / discarded slice an intended promotional-schedule outcome?)

localFindings.description: Sweeps phUSD + rewardToken + promoToken balances and pauses, but leaves promoToken/promoRewardBalance/promoRewardPerSecond/promoPhase/accPromoPerShare untouched. After unpause, _claimRewards' promo leg (L803) still sees promoToken != 0 and attempts safeTransfer of pending promo against a zero balance.
localFindings.status: PRE-EXISTING — already ledgered as V3-M-02 (open). Re-confirmed live at bf42c12; story-024/025 did not touch it.
localFindings.recommendation: Reconcile against ledger, do not re-report as new.

localFindings.description: pauseWithdraw mutates user.amount and totalStaked but never calls _updatePool, so lastRewardTime is left stale. The next _updatePool then divides the ENTIRE elapsed window's stable and phUSD accrual by the post-withdrawal (smaller) totalStaked, over-crediting the remaining stakers for the portion of the window during which the exiting staker's capital was still present. Reachable during Flushing (whenPaused), and during any ordinary pause. Mirrors the Linear-Depletion rate-drift class previously PoC'd in phoenix-nft-staking M-01 / phlimbo Linear-Depletion.
localFindings.impact: Not an insolvency: the stable stream is capped by rewardBalance, so the accelerated accrual only pulls funded value forward in time; the phUSD stream is mint-backed with no cap, so the over-credit there is a genuine (APY-bounded) over-emission. Realistically small — requires a pause and a meaningful pauseWithdraw.
localFindings.recommendation: Call _updatePool() at the head of pauseWithdraw before mutating amount/totalStaked. Note this changes pauseWithdraw's 'does not update pool' documented contract (L521) — that is the intended correction, since the current text presents a defect as a design choice.
localFindings.deferTo: econ-scanner (magnitude of the phUSD over-emission leg), invariant-generator (candidate invariant: accumulator advance must be scaled by the totalStaked in force during the elapsed window)

localFindings.description: abortFlush does not reset flushCursor. Benign at present because beginFlush unconditionally sets flushCursor = 0 (L416), so a stale cursor cannot leak into the next flush. Recorded as a latent coupling: the safety of abortFlush depends entirely on beginFlush's reset, and finalizePromotion's `flushCursor == _stakers.length()` guard would be trivially satisfiable by a stale cursor if that reset were ever removed.
localFindings.recommendation: Zero flushCursor in abortFlush for defence in depth.

externalCalls.notes: Constructor-set, immutable in practice (no setter). Contract must hold an active mint privilege or every phUSD settlement path reverts (SolvencyDetermination §2). Staking token AND reward token.
Constructor-set, no setter. Assumed standard ERC20, no fee-on-transfer, no hooks.

Owner-set per promotion via startPromotion; guarded != 0 && != phUSD && != rewardToken. A promo token with ERC777-style transfer hooks gives the RECIPIENT a callback inside batchClaim's loop — nonReentrant blocks re-entry into batchClaim/stake/withdraw/claim/collectReward, but pauseWithdraw is NOT nonReentrant and IS whenPaused, so it is re-enterable from that callback. Impact is self-limited: pauseWithdraw is msg.sender-only, and the re-entering staker's promoDebt was already aligned at L448 BEFORE the L451 transfer, so the subsequent realignment is consistent. Surfaced for the interaction scanner, not adjudicated here.
Invoked LAST at every call site, after all state writes and inside nonReentrant. A reverting hook bricks stake/withdraw/claim for everyone — owner footgun surface.
finalizePromotion guards != 0; emergencyTransfer does NOT guard != 0.

trustAssumptions: phUSD holds an active mint privilege for this contract; revocation reverts every phUSD settlement path (SolvencyDetermination §2). phUSD's own mint cap/authorization model is OUT OF SCOPE for this profile.
rewardToken and promoToken are standard ERC20: no fee-on-transfer (asserted by balance-delta checks on the promo funding legs), no rebasing, no transfer hooks.
The owner vets each promoToken before startPromotion — the raw-call _tryTransfer and the abi.decode gap (LOCAL-004) are only exploitable via a pathological token.
The hook contract, if set, does not revert and does not re-enter (it is called inside nonReentrant, so re-entry into guarded functions is already blocked).

The migrator address, if set, is a trusted contract — it can withdraw ANY user's stake to itself (withdraw routes principal to msg.sender). This is by design for MigratorV2V3 and is the single largest privilege in the contract; it MUST be un-set (setMigrator(0)) once migration completes.
The owner is non-malicious (Law 3). emergencyTransfer, finalizePromotion's leftover sweep, and the migrator role are all unconditional owner powers and are NOT reported as attack vectors.
handoffToInteractionAnalysis: TREAT AS AXIOM: accPromoPerShare cannot advance while promoPhase == Flushing (story-024 gate at L757, verified over all 11 _updatePool call sites). Any promo-rotation finding premised on mid-flush accumulator advance is REFUTED at this commit.
TREAT AS AXIOM: _stakers membership is frozen while paused; flushCursor is monotone; finalizePromotion requires full coverage.
OPEN FOR INTERACTION ANALYSIS: the promoToken transfer-hook re-entry path into pauseWithdraw (batchClaim L451 -> hook -> pauseWithdraw). Guard analysis above says self-limited; not adjudicated.
OPEN FOR ECON: LOCAL-001 flush-window accrual discard/retroactive-catchup asymmetry; LOCAL-003 pauseWithdraw phUSD over-emission magnitude.
CROSS-CONTRACT: PhlimboV3.stake's MINIMUM_STAKE gate and V3's whenNotPaused gates are hard preconditions for MigratorV2V3.migrate — see MigratorV2V3 profile LOCAL-101/LOCAL-102.
